qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Irreplaceable toll road concessions (407 ETR in Toronto through 2098 and US Express Managed Lanes) possess unreplicable physical rights-of-way and dynamic toll-pricing power. However, consolidated capital efficiency is diluted by heavy capital expenditure, high debt leverage, and low-margin construction operations, resulting in a multi-year median GAAP ROIC of 9.9% (tangible ROIC 10.5%), failing the 12% proof-of-moat hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & ROIC, REJECT). Irreplaceable toll road infrastructure assets (407 ETR in Ontario to 2098, US managed lanes with dynamic pricing) exhibit strong toll-pricing dynamics, but consolidated capital efficiency fails the Munger hurdle with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 9.9% (tangible ROIC 10.5%), diluted by high capital intensity and cyclical construction activities.
qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle capital efficiency fails the 12% GAAP / 15% tangible ROIC hurdle: FY2022 GAAP ROIC 5.7% (tangible 6.0%), FY2023 9.1% (tangible 9.7%), FY2024 37.8% (non-operational asset divestment gain from Heathrow), FY2025 10.65% (tangible 11.23%), yielding a 4-year median GAAP ROIC of 9.86%. Net debt stands at €5.1B (€9.4B LT debt vs €4.2B cash). Under the v6.23 specification, sub-12% consolidated ROIC triggers rejection at Gate 3b.
